evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Missing entirely. Rep jumps straight to confirming existing booking details: 'we have you on our schedule for Thursday October 8th' with no time-box framing or promise of a dependable quote.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Never asked. Rep moves directly into logistics probing without asking 'what are your biggest concerns about this move?'
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides time estimate ('four hours') and mentions $150 travel fee, but does not anchor to a typical range for a one-bedroom move or personalize it to the customer's stated concerns (pull-out couch, construction on site).
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After explaining the $150 travel fee and hourly structure, rep asks 'did you have any questions with regards to our pricing or the estimate, or the moving process at all' — a generic question, not the 'does that feel fair?' close.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Never asked. Call ends with 'thank you so much for your time today sir. You enjoy the rest of your day.' No 'would you like our help with your move?' or booking confirmation.

top_strength: Therese gathered all essential logistics details cleanly — apartment layout, walk distance, special items, floor plan, destination address, construction considerations — and confirmed the box count range without confusion.
coaching_note: This call has no sales structure: skip the quid pro quo open entirely, never surface the customer's concerns, skip pricing framing and the Two Promises, and end without an explicit ask or booking confirmation — rework to follow the seven-section script in order, starting with 'does that sound good to you?' before probing.
